rules.problem: check_for omits glucose, SBP and pulse measurements that the Urgent rule relies on; includes known diabetes as if a sign; inherits asymmetric/allergen-timing/vaccination imprecision.

rules.rule: Measure lying and standing blood pressure after collapse/falls
rules.problem: Omits diastolic drop >=10 criterion; no task for Hb check (<12 woman, <13 man), ECG, substance screen or BP >=140/90.
'Asymmetric' dropped from weakness/numbness; otherwise possible is right for 'consider stroke or TIA'.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis after sudden collapse
rules.problem: Allergen exposure lacks the 'within past few hours' window; any drug/food exposure counts. Possible is correct for 'check for anaphylaxis'.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable orthostatic hypotension after collapse/falls
rules.problem: Diastolic drop >=10 alternative missing, so the probable diagnosis misses diastolic-only drops.
'No' to BP drop only tested on systolic; diastolic omitted. Probable is right ('likely').

rules.rule: Diagnose probable common faint after collapse/falls
rules.problem: Same systolic-only BP test; also the no-symptoms branch (refer if coughing/swallowing/head turning) is not encoded.

Type and priority justified by red box and or-structure matches; imprecisions: asymmetric dropped, vaccination lacks recency, allergen exposure lacks timing. Missing page diagnosis 'anaemia likely' (Hb thresholds) elsewhere.

summary: Most consequential: orthostatic hypotension (and the hyperventilation/faint branches that depend on it) test only the systolic drop >=20, omitting the page's 'or diastolic drop >=10'. Several danger signs are looser than the page: 'asymmetric' weakness/numbness lost, allergen exposure and vaccination lack the recency window. Page diagnosis 'anaemia likely' (Hb <12 woman/<13 man) and the BP >=140/90 and ECG steps are not encoded.
